newsitem.title: CHINA: China accuses stock analyst of falsifying info.
newsitem.headline: China accuses stock analyst of falsifying info.

text.p: China's Guangdong provincial securities authorities have accused a freelance stock commentator of falsifying information on a listed firm in a published article, the Shanghai Securities News said on Tuesday.

The newspaper said an investigation by the authorities found that Tan Chunlin had falsified information in a stock commentary published on July 26 last year on the results of Shenzhen-listed Hainan Haiyao Industrial Co.
This is the first time in the seven-year history of modern China's stock markets that securities authorities have publicly accused a stock analyst of faking information, the newspaper said.

In his commentary, Tan said Hainan Haiyao would report net earnings of 0.4 yuan per share in the first half of last year and predicted the company's earnings per share would hit 1.0 yuan for the whole of 1996, the newspaper said.
In fact, the pharmaceutical company's 1996 net profit plunged to 16.79 million yuan in 1996 against 37.35 million yuan in 1995 with earnings per share falling to 0.1 yuan from 0.24 yuan.
"Investigations by the Guangdong provincial securities authorities found Tan had falsified the information," the newspaper said. "Tan's act misguided investors and created a bad influence."
The newspaper did not give a motive for Tan's action, and did not say which newspaper had published his commentary.
A separate commentary by the newspaper said some stock analysts had used commentaries they wrote to benefit their own stock speculation activities.
"This public criticism of the 'freelance stock analyst' is the first such case in modern China's securities markets," the newspaper said.
"This is a good start. It will help to purify the stock information industry and will promote the healthy development of the stock markets," it said.
